soundness_flags.label: ass:control-floor in def:model-class
soundness_flags.one_line: For two arms, ass:rare-arm-envelope gives pi_t(0)=1-pi_t(1)>=1-C>=eps, so ass:control-floor is redundant in Mclass (though still needed in Mlower).

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 2-3, Conditions 2.2-2.4; p. 5, Theorems 4.2-4.3; p. 6, Corollary 4.4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes a history-dependent policy, action-specific delay law, and potential outcomes independent of the action-delay pair; it proves delayed-DAIPW normality and variance consistency, and Corollary 4.4 assumes pi_t(a)>=C t^{-alpha} plus a polynomial delay tail.
Rewards and delays are generated independently in the stated model, and Assumption 1 imposes a uniform armwise polynomial delay-tail condition; the paper's target is regret.

The paper explicitly distinguishes reward-dependent from reward-independent delays, explains the resulting observed-reward bias, and develops regret algorithms rather than confidence-interval inference.
The paper studies reward-dependent delays and proves near-optimal regret bounds, with matching lower bounds under bounded or sub-Gaussian rewards; it does not claim confidence-interval coverage.

Theorem 2 assumes i.i.d. potential outcomes with nonzero variance, positive assignment probabilities, and variance-convergence/moment conditions, and establishes adaptive AIPW studentized asymptotic normality.
The article derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds for linear functionals in convex regression-function classes under normal errors with known variance.
